title: Customer intake funnel heuristic and runway snapshot for top-account escalations
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We lack a consistent, fast triage that gives product, sales, and CS a shared single-pane view of top-account escalation requests and a defensible runway estimate for roadmap commitments. This causes ad-hoc promises, unclear handoffs to engineering, and missed SLAs.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight intake funnel heuristic and "runway snapshot" that: (1) standardizes initial triage (impact, complexity, compliance risk), (2) yields an immediate recommended runway (quick patch / sprint / multi-quarter), and (3) produces a structured handoff runbook and owner for engineering to act on. Focus on top accounts and escalations for Q2 roadmap planning.
acceptance_criteria: Draft heuristic documented and reviewed by PM, Sales AE lead, CS Director, and Eng lead
Pilot intake form implemented in Zendesk/Hub with required fields capturing impact, data sensitivity, and example workloads
Runway snapshot algorithm returns a recommended delivery band (patch / sprint / Q) for 85% of pilot requests
Handoff runbook includes checklist for security, data access, and test prompts and is attached to every intake ticket
Measured pilot: time-to-triage < 48 hours for 90% of top-account escalations
decision_log: 2026-02-02: Decided to prioritize a rule-based heuristic over an ML model for MVP to ensure explainability for customers and Execs (PMs: Maya, Owen; Eng: Priya)
2026-02-18: Agreed on three primary axes for scoring: customer impact (revenue/active users), implementation complexity (engineering effort), and compliance risk (data sensitivity)
2026-02-26: Chose runway bands: patch (<=2w), sprint (<=8w), multi-sprint/quarter (>=8w) to align with engineering capacity planning
updates: 2026-01-26 - Ticket created by Maya Chen: initial outline and kickoff invite sent to stakeholders
2026-02-02 - PM sync: drafted heuristic and example scoring matrix; Eng raised concern about estimating complexity without a standard rubric
2026-02-10 - Design mock: Lena uploaded a compact intake flow that surfaces mandatory runway fields and auto-populates contact info
2026-02-15 - Pilot scope defined: 6-week pilot for strategic accounts (10 accounts) routed through a dedicated Zendesk form
2026-02-20 - Engineering blocked on access to anonymized workload samples; action: Sales to obtain consent and CS to sanitize examples (assigned to Jonas)
2026-02-28 - Prototype intake form implemented in Zendesk; basic scoring rules implemented as webhook to a simple Lambda
2026-03-03 - First pilot intake submitted (ACME Corp); initial runway snapshot recommended: sprint (6 weeks); Eng requested deeper logs and test prompts
2026-03-07 - Review: stakeholder feedback - Sales wants 'business-critical' flag; Eng wants an automated rough complexity estimator (lines: model size, data transforms)
2026-03-10 - PM decision: add business-critical toggle and a follow-up engineering estimation slot in the intake form; prototype webhook updated
next_steps: Complete engineering rubric for complexity estimation (owner: Priya) by 2026-03-17
CS & Sales to provide sanitized workload examples for 5 pilot accounts by 2026-03-20
Measure pilot KPIs (time-to-triage, runway accuracy vs. actual) during 2026-03-21 to 2026-04-01
Prepare go/no-go brief for roadmap planning sync on 2026-04-05
notes: Trade-offs: we deprioritized a fully ML-driven prioritizer for MVP because model training and explainability would add 6-8 weeks and complicate executive sign-off. Long-term plan: collect pilot data to seed an ML model for nuanced complexity/effort estimates. Open question: do we expose recommended runway to customers or keep internal-only? Security checklist template is in Confluence and needs alignment with Security team before we attach to tickets.
